acceptance: Semantic DOM markers scope compatibility behavior without depending on upstream hashed CSS classes and are cleaned up on disposal.
Header, Chat, Trajectory, sidebar overlay, details column, composer, and Remote access panel pass geometry checks at 360x800, 390x844, and 412x915.
Desktop geometry remains unchanged and focused package checks pass.

stories.given: A 360x800, 390x844, or 412x915 portrait viewport with an existing session and long trajectory labels
stories.goal: Have the session header, Chat and Trajectory views, and their controls fit the visual viewport
stories.role: DSH user opening an existing session from an Android phone
stories.then: The page has no unintended horizontal overflow, important controls remain reachable, labels stay contained, and the sidebar overlays rather than squeezing the conversation
stories.value: Inspect ongoing work without clipped or unreachable content
stories.when: The user opens Chat or Trajectory and expands the sidebar

stories.given: A portrait mobile viewport, a reduced visual viewport height, or a desktop viewport
stories.goal: Keep the composer and Remote access panel readable and operable
stories.role: DSH user working remotely from a phone
stories.then: Input and controls fit without overlap, remain in the visual viewport, and desktop composer geometry remains unchanged
stories.value: Continue a session and manage its private link without switching to a desktop
stories.when: The composer or Remote access panel is displayed

exact_next_action: Implement semantic mobile compatibility markers and scoped responsive CSS, then run focused tests and browser viewport verification.

receipt.outcome: The dsh-remote client applies disposable semantic markers and mobile-only responsive rules so DSH rc.6 sessions, trajectory, sidebar, composer, and Remote panel remain usable on portrait phones without changing desktop layout.
remaining_risks: The compatibility layer targets DSH 0.1.0-rc.6 DOM semantics and should be removed or revalidated when upstream ships mobile support.
A physical Android Chrome device remains the final manual hardware check; Chrome engine and public asset delivery are automated.
